D017-D011_h001.question:
It's been a tough few years since my husband passed away, but lately, something else has really started to consume me. It’s hard to sit here and talk about it, but I feel like I'm constantly being judged. I spend hours in front of the mirror, convinced that one side of my face is completely different from the other – lopsided, you know? No matter how much I try to arrange my hair or angle my head, I can't shake the feeling it's obvious to everyone.

Because of this, getting ready each day for work, even just cleaning houses, has become an ordeal. I have to apply my makeup just so, layering it on thick, and always wear scarves or hats, even indoors sometimes, to try and hide what I see as imperfections. I worry constantly about how I look, thinking about it all day, and I can hear my own critical voice in my head. Other things that used to bother me, like bills or life in general, don't seem to cause the same level of worry anymore; it's all focused on my appearance. It takes up so much of my mental energy; I can barely focus on anything else.

    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
